strengths: Novel and conceptually sound formulation: Adapting Byte Pair Encoding to 3D continuous protein backbone geometry by iteratively merging frequent structural motifs, clustering them via k-medoids, and correcting accumulation of geometric drift through differentiable inverse kinematics on boundary glue angles.

Strong compression and Pareto efficiency: GeoBPE constructs a smooth Pareto frontier between bits-per-residue (BPR) and reconstruction distortion (RMSD, LDDT), achieving substantially lower bitrates than leading VQ-VAE tokenizers like ESM3 and ProToken.

Impressive out-of-distribution robustness and data efficiency: The test/train RMSD ratio on held-out benchmarks (CAMEO, CASP14) remains between 1.16–1.28 (compared to >6x degradation in VQ-VAE baselines), and the tokenizer retains full transfer performance even when fitted on 1% of the pretraining data.

Comprehensive downstream and interpretability evaluation: Evaluated across 12 downstream prediction tasks (24 test splits), showing consistent gains when using the hierarchical merge tree as an inductive bias; the derived tokens also demonstrate strong semantic and geometric alignment with CATH FunFam domain boundaries.
Rigorous algorithmic documentation: The appendix provides exhaustive detail, including 23 detailed algorithms, theoretical complexity analysis, and clear hyperparameter documentation.
weaknesses: Confounding factors in downstream representation transfer: For downstream tasks (Table 1), GeoBPE applies an Up-Down Tree-LSTM over ESM3 leaf representations, whereas discrete PST baselines rely on their own codebook vectors. It is unclear how much of the performance gain stems from the GeoBPE merge tree specifically versus the expressive Tree-LSTM architecture or ESM3 embeddings; an ablation comparing the Tree-LSTM over a random or balanced binary hierarchy would clarify the precise contribution of the learned geometric merge tree.

Preliminary generative performance: In the Small Structure Language Model evaluation (SSLM-Eval, Table 7), the designability (scTM > 0.5) is only 3–4%. While the authors explicitly acknowledge this as a proof-of-concept, it highlights that autoregressive generation over composite motif + glue tokens is still at an early stage compared to state-of-the-art continuous diffusion or large-scale discrete models.

Minor presentation issues: Incomplete sentence at the end of the Abstract ('Code is available at'), typo in Section 3.3 ('Priciple 2'), and unescaped LaTeX formatting in Table 7 header ('\textgreater').

strengths: Principled and novel adaptation of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) to continuous 3D protein geometry, moving beyond standard VQ-VAE/fixed-size structural alphabets by learning variable-length, hierarchical structural primitives.
Clever formulation of boundary 'glue angles' coupled with differentiable forward kinematics (IK refinement) to absorb local quantization drift and preserve global fold integrity.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation covering rate-distortion Pareto frontiers, token efficiency, downstream functional and structural property prediction across 12 tasks/24 splits, generative language modeling, and biological interpretability (CATH FunFams and case studies).
High data efficiency: downstream transfer performance remains robust even when fitting the vocabulary on as little as 1% of the pretraining structures.
Exceptionally clear and thorough algorithmic exposition, with detailed pseudocode and complexity analyses provided in the appendix (Algorithms 1–23).
weaknesses: Disentangling the contribution of the Tree-LSTM versus the GeoBPE tree structure: In downstream transfer experiments, GeoBPE leverages an Up-Down Tree-LSTM over pretrained ESM3 embeddings. It is somewhat unclear how much of the performance gain stems specifically from GeoBPE's geometric merges versus the inductive bias of hierarchical Tree-LSTM aggregation itself (e.g., compared to a balanced binary tree baseline or alternative multi-scale pooling over ESM3).

Generative modeling performance remains modest: While GeoBPE outperforms the discrete VQ-VAE baseline in the small structure LM evaluation (Table 7), absolute designability (3–4%) and average scTM (~0.27) indicate that autoregressive generation over interleaved motif and glue tokens is currently a proof-of-concept and requires scaling up.

The evaluation metric for CATH domain alignment selects the optimal consecutive block of segments via an argmax over all sub-ranges (Section F), which inherently favors fine-grained segmentations and leads to very high baseline scores for random segmentations as well (as shown in parentheses in Table 2).

Scaling to large vocabularies involves quadratic clustering costs (O(M_max^2)) and iterative differentiable inverse kinematics passes, which can be computationally demanding compared to single-pass neural network encoders during the vocabulary construction phase.

strengths: Novel and conceptually sound formulation: Adapting Byte-Pair Encoding to 3D continuous protein backbones is a non-trivial, elegant conceptual step. Discretizing structural fragments into medoid modes while simultaneously mitigating geometric drift through differentiable inverse kinematics (optimizing boundary glue angles under an SE(3) end-frame objective) is well-motivated and mathematically rigorous.

Comprehensive mathematical and algorithmic clarity: The paper establishes a clear formulation of internal coordinates, entry/exit frames, and per-link transformations, accompanied by detailed, explicit pseudocodes for all core procedures (Algos 1–23).

Thorough Pareto efficiency and generalization analysis: GEOBPE demonstrates a favorable compression-versus-distortion tradeoff (BPR vs. RMSD/LDDT) compared to existing vector-quantized PSTs (e.g., ProToken, ESM3 codebook), showing strong out-of-distribution stability on CAMEO and CASP14.

Multi-resolution interpretability: The resulting merge tree provides natural structural decomposition across scales, demonstrating meaningful alignment with secondary structure elements, active sites, and CATH domain annotations.
weaknesses: Confounding factors in downstream transfer evaluation: In Table 1, GEOBPE uses an Up-Down Tree-LSTM (Algo 13) built on top of ESM3 representations, whereas baselines either use their own encoders or raw token features. It is unclear how much of the performance gain stems from the geometric BPE token hierarchy itself versus the additional representational capacity of the bidirectional Tree-LSTM operating over ESM3 representations. A control baseline applying a standard 1D CNN, BiLSTM, or Transformer on top of ESM3 embeddings is missing.

Limited generative performance: In the language modeling generation experiment (Table 7), GEOBPE achieves only 3–4% designability (scTM > 0.5), meaning that the vast majority of generated backbones cannot be refolded by inverse folding models. While the authors note this is a small-scale proof of concept, it leaves the generative utility of the discrete tokens somewhat unproven compared to modern diffusion-based generative models.

Potential metric leniency in CATH domain agreement: In Table 2 / Section F, domain alignment is evaluated by selecting the single best consecutive block of predicted segments that maximizes IoU with each true domain. When a tokenizer generates many fine-grained segments, optimizing the start and end boundary indices across small fragments can inflate overlap metrics (as evidenced by the random-partition baseline also scoring 97.97% recall and 76.82% F1).

Scalability and computational complexity: The reliance on iterative k-medoids on fragment subsets and periodic global differentiable inverse kinematics introduces significant computational overhead compared to purely feedforward neural PSTs, potentially hindering scalability to hundreds of millions of structures (e.g., ESM-scale training corpora).

Presentation and minor editorial inconsistencies: The code availability statement in the abstract is cut short ('Code is available at'), and the method is inconsistently labeled as 'PT-BPE' in Tables 6 and 7 while being termed 'GEOBPE' throughout the text.

strengths: Principled and novel adaptation of Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) to continuous 3D protein backbone structures, introducing an elegant combination of k-medoids motif clustering and differentiable inverse kinematics on boundary glue angles to mitigate cumulative geometric drift.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning multiple axes: compression-distortion tradeoffs (BPR vs. RMSD/LDDT), out-of-distribution generalization on CAMEO and CASP14, token utilization efficiency, downstream transfer on 12 tasks across 24 test splits, and generative language modeling.

Strong compression performance and data efficiency: GEOBPE traces a competitive Pareto front against state-of-the-art vector-quantized tokenizers (e.g., ProToken, ESM3) while demonstrating remarkable sample efficiency (fitting on as little as 1% of pretraining data retains strong performance).

Enhanced biological interpretability and multi-scale representation: the hierarchical merge trees naturally recover recognizable secondary structure elements and functional domains (validated via CATH FunFams, DSSP, and detailed expert case studies), providing symbolic structural tokens with genuine biochemical relevance.
Extensive appendix detailing algorithmic workflows (25 pseudocodes), complexity analyses, hyperparameter sensitivities, and scaling experiments on 550k structures.
weaknesses: Generation capability of the discrete language model is relatively modest: in the small structure language model evaluation (SSLM-Eval), designability (scTM > 0.5) is around 3-4% at base scale and 21% when scaled 10x, which lags behind dedicated continuous diffusion models, though the authors appropriately frame this as a controlled tokenizer benchmark rather than a standalone generative model.

The method is currently restricted to backbone coordinates (N, CA, C), omitting side-chain conformations and joint sequence-structure co-tokenization, which limits its immediate drop-in replacement utility for full-atom multimodal tasks.

Training involves non-negligible computational overhead due to repeated pairwise RMSD matrix computations and iterative differentiable inverse kinematics passes across chains, although subsampling caps and periodic optimization (P=10) effectively mitigate the worst-case complexity.

In the downstream transfer benchmark (Table 1), the performance gain of GEOBPE-TRANSFER relies on pairing the hierarchical merge tree with an Up-Down TreeLSTM over pretrained ESM3 embeddings; separating the exact contribution of the tree inductive bias from the underlying feature extractor requires careful interpretation.

strengths: Novel conceptual framework: Adapting Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) from discrete sequence processing to continuous 3D protein backbone structures is a creative and non-trivial endeavor. The combination of k-medoids clustering of local motifs with differentiable inverse kinematics (IK) over boundary glue angles effectively addresses the challenge of accumulating geometric drift.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The paper thoroughly investigates multiple dimensions of protein tokenization, including rate-distortion trade-offs (BPR vs. RMSD/LDDT), out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization on CAMEO and CASP14, token utilization/perplexity, downstream task transfer across 12 tasks (24 splits), and unconditional backbone generation.

Strong compression and OOD generalization: GEOBPE demonstrates impressive stability on held-out test sets (test/train RMSD ratio of 1.16-1.28 compared to up to 6.4x degradation in standard VQ-VAE baselines) and traces a clear, tunable Pareto front.

Structural and functional interpretability: Unlike latent codebook vectors in VQ-VAEs, GEOBPE tokens represent concrete structural primitives that correspond to observable backbone conformations. The paper backs this up with quantitative alignment to CATH FunFams and secondary structure elements, supported by detailed biological case studies.

Extensive documentation and ablations: The appendix provides exhaustive algorithmic pseudocode (25 algorithms), theoretical computational complexity analysis, empirical wall-clock benchmarks, and extensive sensitivity analyses across hyperparameters.
weaknesses: Confounding factors in downstream transfer evaluation: In Table 1, GEOBPE-TRANSFER uses pre-trained ESM3 embeddings at the leaf level and propagates them through a Tree-LSTM structured by the GEOBPE merge hierarchy. This setup evaluates the hierarchical merge tree as a structured neural architecture on top of a 236M foundation model, whereas several baselines are evaluated on their own latent codes/features. A fairer ablation would compare this against other pooling/graph propagation schemes over ESM3 features, or evaluate GEOBPE's discrete tokens on equal architectural footing.

Complexity of tokenization and autoregressive sequence format: Because the sequence tokenization alternates between motif medoids and three glue-angle bins (a 4-step cycle: motif, theta, omega, phi), the effective sequence length for language modeling is multiplied by four relative to the number of motifs. This mitigates some of the compression benefits when feeding sequences into downstream transformers.

Modest generative performance: Although the small structure language model (SSLM) experiment is presented primarily as a controlled benchmark against VQ-VAEs, the resulting designability scores (3-4% at 7.3M; 21% at 65.9M) remain quite low compared to continuous diffusion-based backbone generators. Generating valid tertiary structures autoregressively from interleaved discrete geometric tokens remains challenging.

Heavy pipeline with numerous interdependent hyperparameters: The method depends on an intricate set of heuristics and parameters (e.g., span-dependent num_p schedules, angular binning strategies, subsampling caps M_max, glue optimization frequencies and loss weights w_R, w_t), which could make practical tuning and re-training on new structural datasets cumbersome.

strengths: Conceptual Novelty: The paper provides a principled, elegant translation of Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) from discrete NLP text to continuous 3D geometric chains. Framing geometric motif merging alongside differentiable inverse kinematics (boundary glue optimization) to prevent structural drift is a creative and mathematically sound formulation.

Comprehensive Empirical Evaluation: The method is rigorously benchmarked across multiple dimensions: rate-distortion Pareto efficiency (BPR vs. RMSD/LDDT), out-of-distribution generalization on CAMEO and CASP14, downstream transfer across 12 tasks (24 splits), generative modeling (SSLM-Eval), and alignment with biological ground truth (CATH FunFams / DSSP secondary structure elements).

Effective Hierarchical Inductive Bias: The use of the hierarchical BPE merge forest as a computational backbone for an Up-Down Tree-LSTM effectively coarsens residue embeddings (e.g., from ESM3) to protein-level and multi-scale representations, achieving notable gains across diverse downstream prediction tasks.

Biological Interpretability: The discovered structural primitives and merge trees demonstrate strong alignment with biological functional motifs (such as transmembrane binding pockets and phospho-binding grooves), providing a level of mechanistic interpretability that standard VQ-VAE latent codes typically lack.

Thorough Documentation and Ablations: The appendix provides exhaustive algorithmic pseudocode (Algorithms 1–25), complexity analyses, wall-clock timing breakdowns, sensitivity sweeps, and hyperparameter guidelines.
weaknesses: Confounding Factors in Downstream Evaluation: In Table 1, GEOBPE-TRANSFER combines pretrained ESM3 embeddings with an Up-Down Tree-LSTM over the GEOBPE merge forest. It is not entirely separated how much of the performance gain is attributable to the specific GEOBPE merge hierarchy versus the expressive power of the bidirectional Tree-LSTM architecture itself (e.g., compared against balanced binary trees, sequence-distance trees, or standard 1D convolutional pooling over ESM3 features).

Computational Overhead of Vocabulary Discovery: Although tokenization of unseen structures is relatively lightweight, vocabulary discovery involves quadratic k-medoids distance matrices (mitigated by subsampling M_max) and iterative differentiable inverse kinematics. While well-analyzed in Appendix J and Table 13, training is notably compute- and CPU-intensive compared to standard sequence BPE.

Limited Standalone Generative Quality: While the generative comparison via SSLM-Eval is a clean benchmark against VQ-VAE tokens, the absolute designability (21% at 65.9M parameters) is modest compared to contemporary continuous diffusion-based generative models (e.g., RFdiffusion, Chroma), highlighting current limitations of discrete autoregressive modeling of backbone geometry.
Minor Formatting Incompleteness: The URL in the abstract ('Code is available at ') and the Reproducibility Statement is left blank/incomplete.
